question: A platform team is restructuring a monolith into three microservices, touching shared data models, service boundaries, and deployment topology, with several viable ways to split the code. Before any files are changed, which approach should the architect direct Claude Code to take?
options: A) Run the restructuring through a CI pipeline with bypassPermissions enabled so the extraction finishes without any manual review step
B) Start in the default accept-edits mode so Claude can begin extracting services immediately and adjust the boundaries as issues surface
C) Enter plan mode so Claude explores the codebase, evaluates the competing service boundaries, and proposes a design before any edit is approved
D) Skip investigation and have Claude pick one service split at random right away, then rely on integration tests to catch structural mistakes later
correct_answers: C) Enter plan mode so Claude explores the codebase, evaluates the competing service boundaries, and proposes a design before any edit is approved
explanations: bypassPermissions removes prompts and safety checks entirely, which is the opposite of the deliberate, reviewable investigation an architectural restructuring calls for.
Accept-edits mode lets Claude write files immediately, so boundary mistakes get baked into multiple files before anyone reviews the overall design.

Correct. Plan mode restricts Claude to read-only exploration and requires an approved plan before edits happen, which is exactly what a multi-file architectural decision with several valid approaches needs to avoid costly rework.
Picking a split without investigation discards the architectural analysis the task needs and pushes discovery of structural errors to test time, after the damage is already spread across files.
